# The GUI, menu by menu

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask docs` from the menus, the actions, the panel help and the shortcut list of the GUI. Do not edit by hand. -->

This page lists everything in the KRAKEN window: the menus, the panels and the keyboard shortcuts. For a walk through the flow, see the [tutorial](tutorial.md). Inside the app, press **F1** for the same help, and **Help > Take the tour** for a short guided tour.

Every menu item and every button says what it does when you hover it. An item that is switched off says why. Every menu item is also in the command palette (**Ctrl+K**), and single-letter shortcuts do nothing while a text box has the focus.

## Menus

On the welcome screen only **File** and **Help** are shown. The other menus appear when a project is open.

### File

Open and import programs and projects, and settings.

| Item | What it does | Shortcut |
|---|---|---|
| Open program... | Import an executable or library into a new project | `Ctrl+O` |
| Open project... | Open a KRAKEN project folder | `Ctrl+Shift+O` |
| Open recent | Projects you opened before. |  |
| Clear recent projects | Empty the list of recently opened projects |  |
| Open demo project | Try KRAKEN on a small built-in program |  |
| Close project | Stop working on this project and go back to the start | `Ctrl+W` |
| Settings... | Engine paths, theme, daemon status and setup | `Ctrl+,` |
| Quit | Close KRAKEN. Your work is already saved | `Ctrl+Q` |

### Edit

Undo, rename, retype and comment.

| Item | What it does | Shortcut |
|---|---|---|
| Undo my last change | Reverse the most recent edit you made | `Ctrl+Z` |
| Rename this function | Give the function you are reading a better name | `N` |
| Change type... | Set the type of the data or function at the cursor | `Y` |
| Edit function signature... | Fix the return type and parameters of this function |  |
| Add a comment to this function | Leave a note for yourself or your team |  |
| Comment at this address... | Leave a note on the line at the cursor | `;` |
| Search commands... | Find any action or command by typing part of its name | `Ctrl+K` |

|---|---|---|

## Panels

Panels live in tabs. Drag a tab to move it, and show any panel from the **View** menu. Right-click a tab and choose **Help for this panel** (or press **F1** in the panel) for the help page.

### Functions

Every function KRAKEN found in the program. Click one to read it.

A function is a named chunk of code that does one job. This list holds every function KRAKEN found. Names like FUN_00401340 are placeholders: nobody has named them yet, so renaming them as you understand them is the heart of the work.

How to use it:

- Click a function to open it in the Decompiler, the Listing and the Graph.
- Type in the filter box to narrow the list. Press Escape to clear it.
- Tick "Hide library stubs" to leave out the small jump entries for imported functions.
- Select a function and press N to rename it.

Shortcuts here: `Ctrl+L` search functions; `N` rename the name under the pointer, or this function; `Up / Down, Enter` move through a list and open the row.

### Decompiler

The selected function rewritten as readable C-like code. Click a call to follow it.

The decompiler guesses what the original source code looked like and shows it as C-like pseudocode. It is easier to read than assembly, but it is a reconstruction, so treat odd-looking details with suspicion.

How to use it:

- Click a name to highlight every place it is used.
- Click a call to follow it. Use Alt+Left to come back.
- Press N on a name to rename it, Y to change its type and ; to add a comment.
- Right-click for more: references, bookmarks, ask the assistant.

Shortcuts here: `N` rename the name under the pointer, or this function; `Y` change the type at the cursor; `;` comment at the cursor; `X` show what refers to the address under the pointer; `Ctrl+D` bookmark the address at the cursor; `Alt+Left` go back; `Alt+Right` go forward again.

### Hex

The raw bytes of the program, as hexadecimal numbers and text.

The raw bytes of the program, shown as hexadecimal numbers with their text on the right. Useful for spotting strings and data that the decompiler does not explain.

How to use it:

- Scroll to move through memory. The view follows the function you open.
- Click a byte to select it. The selection is shown at the top right.
- Use the Show box to jump to a section, such as the code or the data.

Shortcuts here: `G` go to an address, a function or a symbol; `Ctrl+D` bookmark the address at the cursor.

### Listing

The machine instructions behind the code, one per line.

The machine instructions behind the code, one per line. Each line is a mnemonic (what to do) and operands (what to do it to). Hover a mnemonic in learn mode for a plain explanation.

How to use it:

- Click a line to put the cursor on it. Double-click a jump or call to follow it.
- Press Space to swap with the Graph.
- Press N, Y, ; or X on a line to rename, retype, comment or list references.

Shortcuts here: `Space` swap between the listing and the graph; `N` rename the name under the pointer, or this function; `Y` change the type at the cursor; `;` comment at the cursor; `X` show what refers to the address under the pointer; `P` create a function at the cursor; `Ctrl+D` bookmark the address at the cursor.

### Graph

The same code as boxes joined by arrows. Space swaps it with the listing.

The same function drawn as boxes of instructions joined by arrows. Each box runs from top to bottom without a decision; the arrows are the decisions and jumps. Loops and if-else shapes are easier to see here than in a long list.

How to use it:

- Scroll to move around the graph.
- Press F to fit the whole graph in the panel.
- Click a box to put the cursor in it.

Shortcuts here: `F` fit the graph to the panel; `Space` swap between the listing and the graph.

### Xrefs

Who calls this function, what it calls, and what refers to any address.

Cross-references show how pieces of the program connect. For the function you are reading you see its callers (who uses it) and its callees (what it uses). For any address you can list everything that points at it.

How to use it:

- Switch between callers and callees with the buttons at the top.
- Click a row to jump to it.
- Press X on a name or an address in the code to list what refers to it.

Shortcuts here: `X` show what refers to the address under the pointer; `Alt+Left` go back.

### Strings

Text found inside the program. Double-click one to see what uses it.

Readable text found inside the program: messages, file names, URLs, format strings. Strings are often the quickest clue to what a function does.

How to use it:

- Type in the filter box to find a word.
- Double-click a string to see which code refers to it.
- Use Up and Down to move through the list.

Shortcuts here: `Up / Down, Enter` move through a list and open the row.

### Imports / Exports

What the program borrows from libraries, and what it makes available.

Imports are the functions the program borrows from system libraries, such as file, network and memory functions. They tell you what the program can do. Exports are the functions it offers to others, which is how a library is used.

How to use it:

- Type in the filter box to find a name.
- Double-click a row to see the code that uses it.
- Look at the exports first when you open a library (a .dll or .so).

Shortcuts here: `Up / Down, Enter` move through a list and open the row.

### Search

Find names, strings, byte patterns or instructions anywhere in the program. Ctrl+Shift+F.

Search looks through the whole program, not only the function you are reading. Pick what to look for (names, strings, bytes or instructions), type, and press Enter. Each result is a place you can jump to.

How to use it:

- Press Ctrl+Shift+F to open the tab.
- Choose the kind of search, then type and press Enter or click Search.
- Click a result to go there.

Shortcuts here: `Ctrl+Shift+F` search names, strings, bytes or instructions; `G` go to an address, a function or a symbol.

### Bookmarks

Places you or an agent marked to come back to, with notes. Ctrl+D adds one.

Bookmarks are places you want to remember, each with an optional note. You and the assistant can both add them. They are saved in the project.

How to use it:

- Press Ctrl+D on a line to bookmark it.
- Click a bookmark to go there.
- Remove one you no longer need. The program itself is not changed.

Shortcuts here: `Ctrl+D` bookmark the address at the cursor.

### History

Every change made to this project, who made it, and a way to undo it.

A log of every change to this project: who made it, when, and a way to undo it. Nothing the assistant does is permanent.

How to use it:

- Each row says what changed and who did it (you or an agent run).
- Use Undo on a row to reverse that change.
- Press Ctrl+Z to undo your last change without opening this tab.

Shortcuts here: `Ctrl+Z` undo your last change.

### Proposals

Changes suggested by AI assistants that wait for your approval.

When the assistant wants to change something you or someone else already set, it asks first. Proposals wait here until you accept or reject them.

How to use it:

- Read the old value and the suggested one.
- Accept to apply it, or reject to throw it away.

### Assistant

Ask the assistant (an AI model or a terminal agent) about this program in plain language.

Ask questions about this program in plain language. The assistant reads the code through the same tools you use, shows each step, and asks before overwriting your work.

How to use it:

- Type a question and press Enter.
- Watch the steps it takes. Each one is a command you could run yourself.
- Use AI > Automate to let it work through the whole flow.

### Rewrite

Rewrite functions in Rust, check each against the original, and export what you accept.

The Rewrite tab turns functions into Rust and checks every result against the original program. A rewrite is only accepted when it behaves like the original on the tests. Accepted code can be exported as a Rust project.

How to use it:

- Open Rewrite > Rewrite in Rust to start the step-by-step wizard.
- Review each function's plan, translation and test result in this tab.
- Accept the ones you trust, then export and build.

### AI Activity

Which AI work runs, on which model, what it has cost so far, and a Stop button for each.

Every piece of AI work on this project shows here: rewrite jobs started from this window, from the command line or by an agent, and the assistant's runs in this window. Each row says which model it asks, who started it, how many model calls it made and an estimate of the cost. Terminal agents are billed by their own subscription; local models are free.

How to use it:

- Press Stop on a row to end that work. What it finished is kept.
- Click the AI chip in the top bar to come here while work runs.
- Set limits and a daily budget in Settings > AI.

## Keyboard shortcuts

| Keys | What it does | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `Ctrl+O` | Open a program (import it into a new project) | Anywhere |
| `Ctrl+Shift+O` | Open a KRAKEN project folder | Anywhere |
| `Ctrl+W` | Close the project | Project |
| `Ctrl+Q` | Quit KRAKEN | Anywhere |
| `Ctrl+,` | Settings | Anywhere |
| `Ctrl+K or Ctrl+Shift+P` | Search every action and command | Project |
| `Ctrl+/` | This list of shortcuts | Anywhere |
| `F1` | Open help (the topic of the panel you are in) | Anywhere |
| `G` | Go to an address, a function or a symbol | Project |
| `Ctrl+Shift+F` | Search names, strings, bytes or instructions | Project |
| `Ctrl+L` | Search functions | Project |
| `Alt+Left` | Go back | Project |
| `Alt+Right` | Go forward again | Project |
| `N` | Rename the name under the pointer, or this function | Code views |
| `Y` | Change the type at the cursor | Code views |
| `;` | Comment at the cursor | Code views |
| `X` | Show what refers to the address under the pointer | Code views |
| `Ctrl+D` | Bookmark the address at the cursor | Code views |
| `P` | Create a function at the cursor | Code views |
| `Ctrl+Z` | Undo your last change | Project |
| `Space` | Swap between the listing and the graph | Code views |
| `F` | Fit the graph to the panel | Graph |
| `Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab` | Next or previous tab in the focused pane | Project |
| `Ctrl+1 ... Ctrl+9` | Jump to a tab of the focused pane | Project |
| `Up / Down, Enter` | Move through a list and open the row | Lists and palette |
| `Escape` | Close a dialog, menu or the palette | Dialogs |

Press **Ctrl+/** in the app for this list.
